Proposition
[Right polygon identities] \group trigonometrySource: thurston:page-0031, thurston:page-0032, thurston:page-00351. 2.6.10,2.6.17,2.6.18For an all-right hexagon, \[ \cosh C=\frac{\cosh \alpha \cosh \beta +\cosh \gamma }{\sinh \alpha \sinh \beta },\qquad \frac{\sinh A}{\sinh \alpha }=\frac{\sinh B}{\sinh \beta }=\frac{\sinh C}{\sinh \gamma }. \] For an all-right pentagon, $\sinh A\sinh B=\cosh D$.
Proof

\sketch Apply the dual-basis formula to decompositions into right triangles and eliminate intermediate diagonals; the pentagon identity is the corresponding two-triangle calculation, and comparison of the three hexagon expressions gives its sine law.
